carbapenems.name: Meropenem (Merrem®)
carbapenems.dosing: 1-2g IV q8h (extended infusion 3-4h for serious infections)
carbapenems.renalAdjustment: CrCl 26-50: 1g q12h; CrCl 10-25: 500mg q12h; CrCl <10: 500mg q24h; HD: 500mg post-HD
carbapenems.keyWarning: Contraindicated with valproic acid - reduces levels 60-90%
carbapenems.resistanceInfo: Active vs. ESBL, KPC, OXA-48; NOT active vs. NDM/VIM/IMP
carbapenems.drugInteractions: Valproic acid (↓ levels 60-90%), probenecid (↑ levels 50%), warfarin (↑ INR 10-20%)
carbapenems.precautions: CNS toxicity with renal failure, C. difficile risk 3-5%, thrombocytopenia with prolonged use

carbapenems.name: Ertapenem (Invanz®)
carbapenems.spectrum: Similar to meropenem but NO Pseudomonas or Acinetobacter activity
carbapenems.renalAdjustment: CrCl 11-30: 500mg q24h; CrCl ≤10: 250-500mg q48h; HD: 500mg post-HD
carbapenems.keyWarning: Same contraindications as meropenem (valproic acid, carbapenem allergy)
carbapenems.precautions: C. difficile risk 3-5%, avoid in Pseudomonas suspected

carbapenems.name: Doripenem (Doribax®)
carbapenems.dosing: 500mg IV q8h (4h extended infusion for HAP/VAP)
carbapenems.renalAdjustment: CrCl 30-50: 250mg q8h; CrCl <30: 250mg q12h; HD: 250mg q12h + post-HD
carbapenems.precautions: Seizure risk 1-2%, avoid in CNS infections

carbapenems.name: Imipenem-Cilastatin (Primaxin®)
carbapenems.spectrum: Broad Gram-positive and Gram-negative coverage (no MRSA)
carbapenems.keyWarning: Highest seizure risk among carbapenems (3-5%) - AVOID in CNS infections
carbapenems.resistanceInfo: Pseudomonas resistance develops rapidly during therapy
carbapenems.precautions: Cilastatin component required to prevent nephrotoxicity, high nausea incidence (20%)

penicillins.name: Piperacillin-Tazobactam (Zosyn®)
penicillins.spectrum: Reliable anti-pseudomonal activity, good anaerobic coverage
penicillins.dosing: 4.5g IV q6h (extended 4h infusion for serious infections)
penicillins.renalAdjustment: CrCl 20-40: 2.25g q6h; CrCl <20: 2.25g q8h; HD: 2.25g q8h + post-HD
penicillins.precautions: Sodium overload (2.79 mEq Na/g), avoid concurrent vancomycin (↑ nephrotoxicity 3-5x)

penicillins.name: Ampicillin-Sulbactam (Unasyn®)
penicillins.spectrum: Sulbactam inhibits ESBLs and has intrinsic anti-Acinetobacter activity
penicillins.dosing: 3g IV q6h (9g q8h for CRAB infections)
penicillins.renalAdjustment: CrCl 15-29: 1.5-3g q12h; CrCl <15: 1.5-3g q24h; HD: 1.5-3g post-HD
penicillins.resistanceInfo: Unique activity against some ESBLs and Acinetobacter
penicillins.precautions: Rash risk 10% in infectious mononucleosis, C. difficile risk 5-8%

penicillins.name: Penicillin G
penicillins.renalAdjustment: CrCl <10: 2 million units q6h; HD: 2 million units post-HD
penicillins.keyWarning: Hypersensitivity reactions (3-10%), Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction in syphilis
penicillins.resistanceInfo: High resistance in community MRSA, ESBL producers
penicillins.precautions: Test dose for allergy history, potassium content (1.7 mEq/g in K+ salt)

penicillins.name: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate (Augmentin®)
penicillins.renalAdjustment: CrCl 10-30: 500mg/125mg q12h; CrCl <10: 500mg/125mg q24h; HD: 500mg/125mg post-HD
penicillins.keyWarning: Cholestatic jaundice (1-3%), especially with prolonged therapy (>2 weeks)
penicillins.resistanceInfo: NOT active against ESBL producers or MRSA
penicillins.precautions: Allopurinol co-administration ↑ rash risk 3x (not true allergy)

cephalosporins.name: Ceftriaxone (Rocephin®)
cephalosporins.hepaticAdjustment: Reduce dose if severe hepatic impairment + renal dysfunction combined
cephalosporins.keyWarning: Biliary sludge with prolonged use, NEVER co-administer with calcium
cephalosporins.resistanceInfo: NOT active against ESBL producers or MRSA

cephalosporins.name: Cefepime (Maxipime®)
cephalosporins.renalAdjustment: CrCl 30-60: 1-2g q12h; CrCl 11-29: 1-2g q24h; CrCl ≤10: 0.5-1g q24h; HD: 0.5-1g q24h + post-HD
cephalosporins.resistanceInfo: Stable to AmpC but NOT ESBL
cephalosporins.precautions: Neurotoxicity with renal failure, discontinue if myoclonus develops

cephalosporins.name: Ceftazidime-Avibactam (Avycaz®)
cephalosporins.spectrum: Active vs. KPC and OXA-48 CRE
cephalosporins.renalAdjustment: CrCl 31-50: 1.25g q8h; CrCl 16-30: 0.94g q8h; CrCl ≤15: 0.94g q12h; HD: 0.94g q12h + post-HD
cephalosporins.keyWarning: Combine with aztreonam for NDM producers
cephalosporins.precautions: Higher cost ($1,200-1,500/day), not active against NDM

cephalosporins.name: Ceftaroline (Zinifaro®)
cephalosporins.renalAdjustment: CrCl 30-50: 400mg q12h; CrCl <30: 300mg q12h; HD: 300mg q12h + post-HD
cephalosporins.keyWarning: QT prolongation risk (2-3%), monitor ECG in high-risk patients
cephalosporins.resistanceInfo: Not active against ESBL or CRE
cephalosporins.precautions: Cross-reactivity with penicillins 10%, avoid in Pseudomonas suspected

aminoglycosides.name: Gentamicin
aminoglycosides.spectrum: Pseudomonas, ESBL Gram-negative (aminoglycoside activity independent of β-lactamases)
aminoglycosides.renalAdjustment: Requires TDM; adjust interval based on CrCl (CrCl 40-60: 4mg/kg q24h; CrCl 20-40: 3mg/kg q48h)
aminoglycosides.hepaticAdjustment: No adjustment, but avoid in severe liver disease with nephrotoxins
aminoglycosides.precautions: Contraindicated in myasthenia gravis, AVOID in pregnancy

aminoglycosides.name: Tobramycin
aminoglycosides.renalAdjustment: Requires TDM; adjust interval based on CrCl
aminoglycosides.precautions: Inhaled formulation available for CF maintenance (↓ systemic toxicity)

aminoglycosides.name: Amikacin (Amikin®)
aminoglycosides.spectrum: Broadest aminoglycoside spectrum - active vs. most gentamicin-resistant strains
aminoglycosides.dosing: 15-20 mg/kg q24h (HIGH dose due to lower potency)
aminoglycosides.renalAdjustment: Requires TDM; CrCl 30-60: 7.5-10 mg/kg q24h; CrCl <30: 5-7 mg/kg q48h; HD: 5-7 mg/kg post-HD
aminoglycosides.resistanceInfo: Resistance developing in MDR Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter
aminoglycosides.precautions: Baseline audiogram mandatory for therapy >7 days, avoid in pregnancy

fluoroquinolones.name: Levofloxacin (Levaquin®)
fluoroquinolones.renalAdjustment: CrCl 20-49: 750mg then 250mg q24h; CrCl <20: 750mg then 250mg q48h; HD: 750mg then 500mg q48h
fluoroquinolones.keyWarning: Tendon rupture risk (0.1-1%), QT prolongation, photosensitivity (5-10%)
fluoroquinolones.resistanceInfo: Increasing resistance in E. coli UTIs
fluoroquinolones.drugInteractions: Multivalent cations (↓ absorption 90%), warfarin (↑ INR 20-50%), corticosteroids (↑ tendon rupture)
fluoroquinolones.precautions: AVOID in age >60 with vascular disease (aortic aneurysm/dissection risk), AVOID in pregnancy/children <18

fluoroquinolones.name: Ciprofloxacin (Cipro®)
fluoroquinolones.renalAdjustment: CrCl 30-50: 200-400mg q12h; CrCl <30: 200-400mg q24h; HD: 200-400mg post-HD
fluoroquinolones.keyWarning: More CNS effects than levofloxacin, tendon rupture risk
fluoroquinolones.drugInteractions: Tizanidine (contraindicated - CYP1A2 inhibition), theophylline (↑ levels 50%), warfarin (↑ INR)
fluoroquinolones.precautions: Strong CYP1A2 inhibitor, avoid in elderly >60 years, steroid users, transplant recipients

fluoroquinolones.name: Moxifloxacin (Avelox®)
fluoroquinolones.spectrum: Active against anaerobes and atypicals, NO Pseudomonas
fluoroquinolones.hepaticAdjustment: Use with caution in severe impairment (Child-Pugh C)
fluoroquinolones.keyWarning: HIGHEST QT prolongation risk among quinolones - ECG mandatory
fluoroquinolones.resistanceInfo: Poor urinary excretion - NOT for UTIs
fluoroquinolones.precautions: Monitor ECG if cardiac risk factors, avoid in patients on antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics

glycopeptides.name: Vancomycin (Vancocin®)
glycopeptides.spectrum: Gram-positive ONLY (MRSA, MSSA, streptococci, VSE enterococci)
glycopeptides.renalAdjustment: CrCl 30-50: 15-20 mg/kg q24h; CrCl 10-29: 10-15 mg/kg q24h; CrCl <10: 10-15 mg/kg q48-72h; HD: 10-15 mg/kg post-HD
glycopeptides.precautions: Infuse over ≥60 minutes to prevent Red Man Syndrome, TDM mandatory

glycopeptides.name: Teicoplanin (Targocid®)
glycopeptides.spectrum: Gram-positive ONLY including VRE (VanB, VanC, VanE, VanG)
glycopeptides.dosing: 6-12 mg/kg loading (q12h x3), then 6-12 mg/kg q24h maintenance
glycopeptides.renalAdjustment: CrCl 40-60: 6 mg/kg q48h; CrCl <40: 6 mg/kg q72h; HD: 6 mg/kg post-HD (removed 40-65% by HD)
glycopeptides.precautions: Long half-life (70-100h) allows once-daily dosing, TDM recommended (target trough 15-30 mg/L)

glycopeptides.name: Daptomycin (Cubicin®)
glycopeptides.precautions: Stop statins during therapy, monitor CK weekly, contraindicated in pneumonia

tetracyclines.name: Doxycycline (Vibramycin®)
tetracyclines.spectrum: MRSA, MSSA, atypicals (Rickettsia, Ehrlichia, Chlamydia), some anaerobes
tetracyclines.keyWarning: EXTREME photosensitivity (30-50%), tooth discoloration in children/pregnancy
tetracyclines.precautions: TAKE WITH FULL GLASS WATER, stay upright 30 min to prevent esophageal ulceration

tetracyclines.name: Tigecycline (Tygacil®)
tetracyclines.spectrum: Broadest spectrum - MRSA, VRE, ESBL, anaerobes, atypicals
tetracyclines.keyWarning: BLACK BOX: ↑ mortality vs. comparators (10-15%), reserve for no alternatives
tetracyclines.precautions: Prophylactic antiemetics recommended (nausea/vomiting 30%), NOT for bacteremia or VAP

macrolides.name: Azithromycin (Klacid®)
macrolides.renalAdjustment: No adjustment needed for mild-moderate impairment
macrolides.keyWarning: QT prolongation (1-3%), hepatotoxicity with prolonged use
macrolides.drugInteractions: CYP3A4 substrates (↑ levels), warfarin (↑ INR 30-50%), digoxin (↑ levels)
macrolides.precautions: Monitor ECG in cardiac risk patients, avoid with other QT-prolonging drugs

macrolides.name: Clarithromycin
macrolides.spectrum: Streptococci, H. influenzae, atypicals, some MSSA
macrolides.hepaticAdjustment: Severe hepatic impairment + renal impairment: CONTRAINDICATED
macrolides.drugInteractions: CYP3A4 substrates (strong inhibitor), statins (↑ rhabdomyolysis risk 10x)
macrolides.precautions: AVOID with simvastatin/lovastatin, monitor for QT prolongation

sulfonamides.name: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (Septrin®)
sulfonamides.renalAdjustment: CrCl 15-30: 160/800mg q24h; CrCl <15: 160/800mg q48h; HD: 160/800mg post-HD
sulfonamides.hepaticAdjustment: Use caution in severe hepatic impairment
sulfonamides.resistanceInfo: High resistance in E. coli UTIs (20-40%), NOT active against Pseudomonas
sulfonamides.drugInteractions: Warfarin (↑ INR 50-100%), phenytoin (↑ levels), methotrexate (↑ toxicity)
sulfonamides.precautions: Folinic acid supplementation for prolonged therapy, avoid in G6PD deficiency

others.name: Linezolid (Zyvox®)
others.drugInteractions: SSRIs/SNRIs (serotonin syndrome), MAO inhibitors (contraindicated), tyramine-rich foods (hypertensive crisis)
others.precautions: Monitor CBC weekly, limit duration to ≤14 days, screen for serotonergic agents

others.name: Metronidazole (Flagyl®)
others.keyWarning: DISULFIRAM REACTION with alcohol (up to 72 hours after last dose)
others.precautions: AVOID ALL ALCOHOL during therapy + 72h after, monitor for peripheral neuropathy with prolonged use

others.name: Clindamycin (Cleocin®)
others.keyWarning: HIGHEST C. difficile risk (5-20%) - limit to ≤7 days
others.precautions: Limited duration (≤7 days), use metronidazole for routine anaerobic coverage, avoid if C. diff history

mdr.name: MDR Infections Overview
mdr.spectrum: Multidrug-Resistant organisms resistant to ≥3 antibiotic classes
mdr.keyWarning: Monotherapy failure rate 15-50% depending on organism and site
mdr.resistanceInfo: Combination therapy ↓ mortality 39% in CRE bacteremia

mdr.name: ESBL + Aminoglycoside-Resistant
mdr.keyWarning: Tigecycline monotherapy failure rate 30-50% due to resistance emergence
mdr.resistanceInfo: 80-90% cure with combination vs. 60-70% with single agent
mdr.precautions: Extended spectrum beta-lactamase producers with aminoglycoside resistance

mdr.name: CRE Bloodstream Infections
mdr.dosing: Meropenem-vaborbactam 4g q8h OR Ceftazidime-avibactam + Aztreonam 2g q8h
mdr.keyWarning: Always confirm resistance mechanism before selecting therapy
mdr.resistanceInfo: 70-80% clinical cure with combination vs. 45-55% with monotherapy
mdr.precautions: TDM for vancomycin if combined, monitor for C. difficile

mdr.name: MDR Acinetobacter Solutions
mdr.dosing: High-dose ampicillin-sulbactam 9g IV q8h + minocycline 200mg IV q12h
mdr.renalAdjustment: CrCl 30-50: 6g q8h + minocycline 100mg q12h; CrCl <30: 3g q8h + minocycline 100mg q24h
mdr.keyWarning: Sulbactam component provides unique anti-Acinetobacter activity
mdr.precautions: Renal monitoring essential (high sodium load), phlebitis common

esbl.name: ESBL Definition & Epidemiology
esbl.spectrum: ESBLs exclusively produced by GRAM-NEGATIVE bacteria (Enterobacteriaceae)
esbl.keyWarning: Plasmid-encoded - rapid horizontal transmission between bacteria
esbl.resistanceInfo: CTX-M (80% of ESBLs in US), SHV, TEM enzymes; NOT hydrolyzed by carbapenems
esbl.precautions: Risk factors: prior antibiotic exposure, healthcare exposure, travel to endemic areas

esbl.name: ESBL Empiric Therapy
keyUses: Septic shock with ESBL risk factors
esbl.dosing: Meropenem 2g IV q8h over 3h infusion (extended) for first 48 hours
esbl.keyWarning: Empiric coverage crucial in high-risk patients
esbl.resistanceInfo: 85-95% clinical cure when started early in septic shock
esbl.precautions: Assess for de-escalation after 48h if cultures negative

esbl.name: ESBL Treatment Guidelines
esbl.dosing: Carbapenems for severe infections; TMP-SMX/fluoroquinolones for susceptible UTIs
esbl.keyWarning: Avoid cephalosporins for ESBL infections - high failure rates
esbl.resistanceInfo: Meropenem 85-95% clinical cure when started early in septic shock
esbl.precautions: Duration: 7 days for uncomplicated UTIs, 14 days for bacteremia, source control essential

resistance.name: KPC Carbapenemase (Class A)
resistance.keyWarning: Always confirm resistance mechanism before selecting therapy
resistance.precautions: Use when MIC ≤4 mg/L, not active against MBL producers

resistance.name: Metallo-Beta-Lactamases (MBL - NDM/VIM)
resistance.dosing: Ceftazidime-avibactam 2.5g q8h + Aztreonam 2g q8h (both extended infusion)
resistance.keyWarning: Avibactam does not inhibit MBLs; aztreonam provides coverage
resistance.resistanceInfo: 70-80% clinical cure in compassionate use programs
resistance.precautions: Confirm NDM/VIM production before use, consider adding colistin for deep infections

resistance.name: Tigecycline Resistance
resistance.dosing: Sulbactam 9g q8h + minocycline + colistin for A. baumannii
resistance.keyWarning: NEVER use tigecycline monotherapy for severe infections
resistance.resistanceInfo: Efflux pump overexpression (AcrAB-TolC) and tet(X4) gene are common mechanisms
resistance.precautions: Therapeutic drug monitoring for colistin (nephrotoxic), monitor for C. difficile

stewardship.name: Antimicrobial Stewardship Principles
stewardship.dosing: Review all antibiotics at 48-72 hours for de-escalation
stewardship.keyWarning: Longer duration increases resistance risk and side effects
stewardship.resistanceInfo: Appropriate duration ↓ mortality and resistance development
stewardship.precautions: Document indication, expected duration, and planned review at 48-72h

stewardship.name: Extended Infusion Protocols
stewardship.keyWarning: Standard short infusions may fail to achieve PK/PD targets in severe infections
stewardship.resistanceInfo: Extended infusion improves outcomes in sepsis by 20-30%
stewardship.precautions: Compatibility with IV fluids, stability during extended infusion

stewardship.name: Therapeutic Drug Monitoring
stewardship.dosing: Target AUC/MIC 400-600 for vancomycin; peaks/troughs for aminoglycosides
stewardship.keyWarning: TDM essential for narrow therapeutic index drugs
stewardship.resistanceInfo: Proper dosing prevents subtherapeutic exposure and resistance development
stewardship.precautions: Timing of blood draws critical for accurate interpretation, use validated assays

stewardship.name: Critical Care Dosing Strategies
stewardship.dosing: "Front-loading" full dose within first 48h, then adjust based on renal function
stewardship.keyWarning: Standard doses often subtherapeutic in sepsis due to ↑ volume of distribution
stewardship.resistanceInfo: Hydrophilic drugs (β-lactams, aminoglycosides, glycopeptides) require higher loading doses
stewardship.precautions: Monitor for therapeutic failure at 48h, adjust based on measured CrCl

pregnancy.name: Penicillins in Pregnancy
pregnancy.spectrum: Group B streptococcus, E. coli, MSSA
pregnancy.dosing: Amoxicillin 500mg PO q8h or Penicillin G 5 million units IV q4h
pregnancy.safety: FDA Category B - No evidence of fetal risk
pregnancy.precautions: Skin testing if prior reaction, monitor for ampicillin rash in mononucleosis

pregnancy.name: Cephalosporins in Pregnancy
pregnancy.safety: FDA Category B - No evidence of fetal risk
pregnancy.keyWarning: Low risk of biliary sludge with prolonged use
pregnancy.resistanceInfo: NOT active against ESBL or MRSA
pregnancy.precautions: Avoid in 3rd trimester if neonatal hyperbilirubinemia risk

pregnancy.name: Clindamycin & Azithromycin
pregnancy.dosing: Clindamycin 900mg IV q8h or Azithromycin 500mg IV daily
pregnancy.keyWarning: Clindamycin: C. difficile risk (5-10%); Azithromycin: QT prolongation
pregnancy.resistanceInfo: Clindamycin resistance in GBS 10-15%; azithromycin resistance in S. pneumoniae 30-40%
pregnancy.precautions: Azithromycin preferred over erythromycin (less GI side effects)

pregnancy.name: Drugs to AVOID in Pregnancy
pregnancy.safety: CONTRAINDICATED: Fluoroquinolones (Category C), Tetracyclines (Category D), Aminoglycosides (Category D for gentamicin/tobramycin)
pregnancy.keyWarning: Fluoroquinolones: cartilage toxicity; Tetracyclines: tooth discoloration, bone growth inhibition; Aminoglycosides: fetal ototoxicity
pregnancy.precautions: Aminoglycosides only if absolutely necessary (e.g., MDR TB); monitor fetal hearing after birth

prophylaxis.name: Surgical Site Infection Prophylaxis
prophylaxis.spectrum: Skin flora (S. aureus, S. epidermidis), enteric organisms
prophylaxis.dosing: Cefazolin 2g IV (3g if BMI >30) within 60 min before incision
prophylaxis.duration: Single dose for most procedures; redose q4h for cefazolin during long procedures
prophylaxis.resistanceInfo: MRSA coverage not needed for routine prophylaxis
prophylaxis.precautions: Extend to 24h for cardiac, orthopedic, and major vascular procedures

prophylaxis.name: Endocarditis Prophylaxis
keyUses: Dental procedures with manipulation of gingival tissue
prophylaxis.keyWarning: Indications narrowed since 2007 (only highest risk cardiac conditions)
prophylaxis.resistanceInfo: Penicillin resistance in viridans streptococci rare (<5%)
prophylaxis.precautions: Only for patients with prosthetic cardiac valves, previous IE, congenital heart disease

prophylaxis.name: Travel Prophylaxis
prophylaxis.dosing: Doxycycline 100mg PO daily starting 1-2 days before travel; Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO daily for high-risk travel
prophylaxis.duration: Doxycycline: entire stay + 4 weeks after; Ciprofloxacin: during high-risk exposure only
prophylaxis.keyWarning: Doxycycline: photosensitivity; Ciprofloxacin: tendon rupture risk
prophylaxis.resistanceInfo: Chloroquine resistance widespread in P. falciparum
prophylaxis.precautions: Malaria prophylaxis must continue after return, sunscreen with doxycycline

prophylaxis.name: Close Contact Prophylaxis
prophylaxis.spectrum: N. meningitidis, B. pertussis, S. pyogenes
prophylaxis.dosing: Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO single dose (meningococcal); Azithromycin 500mg PO daily x5d (pertussis)
prophylaxis.keyWarning: Secondary cases can occur within 7 days if prophylaxis delayed
prophylaxis.resistanceInfo: Macrolide resistance in B. pertussis increasing (10-15%)
prophylaxis.precautions: Treat entire household for pertussis, check vaccination status

preop.name: Cardiac Surgery
preop.dosing: Cefazolin 2g IV (3g if BMI >30) within 60 min before incision
preop.alternatives: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV if MRSA colonization or β-lactam allergy

preop.name: Orthopedic Surgery
preop.dosing: Cefazolin 2g IV (3g if BMI >30) within 60 min before incision
preop.duration: 24 hours post-op (24h for clean cases, 48-72h for trauma/contaminated)
preop.alternatives: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV if MRSA history or β-lactam allergy
preop.keyWarning: MRSA decolonization (mupirocin + chlorhexidine) pre-op ↓ SSI by 40%
preop.precautions: Consider adding vancomycin for revision arthroplasty or MRSA history

preop.name: Gastrointestinal Surgery
preop.dosing: Cefoxitin 2g IV or Piperacillin-tazobactam 3g IV within 60 min before incision
preop.alternatives: Ertapenem 1g IV if high ESBL risk
preop.keyWarning: Mechanical bowel prep + oral antibiotics ↓ SSI by 60% in colorectal surgery
preop.precautions: Oral antibiotic component: Neomycin/erythromycin base the day before

preop.name: Gynecologic Surgery
preop.spectrum: Enteric Gram-negative rods, anaerobes, group B strep
preop.dosing: Cefazolin 2g IV + Metronidazole 500mg IV within 60 min before incision
preop.alternatives: Clindamycin 900mg IV + Gentamicin 5mg/kg IV if β-lactam allergy
preop.keyWarning: Single dose for C-section after cord clamping ↓ neonatal exposure
preop.precautions: Redose q3-4h for long procedures, consider azithromycin for C-section (↓ endometritis 50%)

terminology.name: MDR (Multidrug-Resistant)
terminology.definition: Resistant to ≥3 antibiotic classes (e.g., MDR Pseudomonas, MDR Acinetobacter)
terminology.clinicalImportance: Limited treatment options, higher mortality (20-50% vs. 5-10% for susceptible)
terminology.detection: Antibiotic susceptibility testing showing resistance to multiple classes
terminology.prevalence: Increasing worldwide, 10-25% of Gram-negative isolates in hospitals
terminology.keyStrategies: Combination therapy, source control, therapeutic drug monitoring

terminology.name: ESBL (Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase)
terminology.definition: Enzymes that hydrolyze penicillins and cephalosporins but not carbapenems
terminology.clinicalImportance: Treatment failure with cephalosporins (30-40% failure rate)
terminology.detection: Phenotypic tests (ceftazidime/clavulanate synergy), molecular PCR for genes
terminology.prevention: Avoid unnecessary cephalosporin use, infection control for ESBL carriers
terminology.prevalence: E. coli (10-15%), K. pneumoniae (20-30%) in US hospitals
terminology.keyStrategies: Carbapenems for severe infections, TMP-SMX or nitrofurantoin for susceptible UTIs

terminology.name: MIC (Minimum Inhibitory Concentration)
terminology.definition: Lowest concentration of antibiotic that prevents visible bacterial growth
terminology.clinicalImportance: Guides dosing strategy (standard vs. high dose), predicts clinical success
terminology.detection: Broth microdilution, Etest, automated systems (VITEK, BD Phoenix)
terminology.interpretation: Susceptible (S), Intermediate (I), Resistant (R) based on CLSI/EUCAST breakpoints
terminology.limitations: In vitro measure, may not reflect in vivo conditions (protein binding, tissue penetration)
terminology.keyStrategies: Dose optimization based on MIC (e.g., high-dose extended infusion for high MIC organisms)

terminology.name: Culture-Guided Therapy
terminology.definition: Using microbiology results to guide antibiotic selection and de-escalation
terminology.clinicalImportance: Optimizes antibiotic use, reduces resistance development, improves outcomes
terminology.detection: Blood cultures, tissue cultures, urine cultures with susceptibility testing
terminology.timing: Obtain cultures BEFORE starting antibiotics when possible (except septic shock)
terminology.stewardship: Review cultures at 48-72h for de-escalation or discontinuation
terminology.limitations: Slow turnaround (24-72h), false negatives with prior antibiotic use
terminology.keyStrategies: Empiric therapy based on site + local resistance patterns, then de-escalate to targeted therapy
